roomsize.description: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

rootNotes.description: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

round.description: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

rsize.description: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

run.description: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

s.description: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

saw2.description: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

scale.description: Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

scaleTrans.description: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

scaleTranspose.description: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

scope.description: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

scramble.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random.

scrub.description: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

seed.description: Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time, so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values.

seg.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

segment.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

seq.description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

seqPLoop.description: Similarly to arrange, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.

sequenceP.description: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

setcpm.description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

shape.description: (Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.

shrink.description: *Experimental* Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times.

shuffle.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order.

sine2.description: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

size.description: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

slice.description: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers.

slow.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
slow.example: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

slowChunk.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

slowcat.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

slowcatPrime.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

slowchunk.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

someCyclesBy.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis.

sometimes.description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

sometimesBy.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability.

sound.description: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

source.description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

sparsity.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
sparsity.example: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

spectrum.description: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

speed.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

splice.description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

spread.description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
spread.example: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

square2.description: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

squeeze.description: Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given pattern of integers.
squeeze.example: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

squiz.description: Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter.

src.description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

stack.description: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

stepalt.description: *Experimental* Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'.

stepcat.description: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.

strans.description: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

stretch.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

striate.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

struct.description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:

stut.description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

stutWith.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

stutwith.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

sub.description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.

superimpose.description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

sus.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

sustain.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

swingBy.description: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice.

sysex.description: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

sysexdata.description: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

sysexid.description: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

sz.description: Sets the room size of the reverb, see room. When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

tag.description: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering.

take.description: *Experimental* Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest).

time.description: A signal representing the cycle time.

timeCat.description: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.

timecat.description: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.

timeline.description: Allows you to switch a pattern between different 'timelines'.

toBipolar.description: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1.

tour.description: *Experimental* Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions.
tour.example: "[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()

trans.description: Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.

transient.description: Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients and sustains

transpose.description: Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.

unison.example: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

unit.description: Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds).

useRNG.description: Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would use useRNG('legacy'), which remains the default.
